items.q: Why analogize a voice agent to a self-driving stack?
items.a: **Perception** is transcription, **planning** is the LLM, **controls** is TTS. Cascaded layers let you keep **frontier intelligence** and hide latency in the harness instead of shrinking the brain.

items.q: What is EliseAI unwilling to sacrifice for speed?
items.a: **Intelligence.** The talk is a set of tricks on ASR, tools, and TTS so a **slow frontier LLM** still feels real-time.

items.q: How can transcription be both fast and accurate?
items.a: A **fast streaming model** (Flux) starts the pipeline. A **slower batch model** (Scribe V2) confirms, **cancels** if new audio beats the old hypothesis, or **corrects** using the question (name vs date of birth).

items.q: How do they avoid an extra LLM inference for tool calling?
items.a: **Background agents** extract name/DOB, including **phonetic matching**, and **inject tool traces** so the speaker thinks it made the call. Incomplete partials do not fire. A "please spell it" draft is **canceled** once the tools land.

items.q: When does the user actually hear a reply?
items.a: Generation starts on **every streaming detection**. Audio is **held until the user finishes speaking**, then released — or retriggered if context changed.

items.q: What is a TTS prefix cache?
items.a: After about **three words**, replay cached audio for common openings (**you said your name is**). **Cartesia** still synthesizes the **full sentence** for prosody; playback **suppresses the prefix already heard** and plays only the unique tail.

items.q: Where does EliseAI apply this harness?
items.a: **Housing and healthcare** — "life's most critical areas." NYC HQ, Bay Area expansion, not a generic SF chatbot. The demo is an **OBGYN ultrasound scheduler**.
